A regression in remote HTML extraction or relative-URL absolutization (e.g. ports being dropped or duplicated slashes on nonstandard ports) would ship undetected and corrupt every imported article's links and images; only the import happy path and job gating are exercised by topic_embed_spec.rb and poll_feed_spec.rb.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior that is largely untested: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches remote HTML via `open(url).read` and runs `Readability::Document` (no spec hits this path), `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` builds `prefix` including nonstandard ports and strips leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`), but `topic_embed_spec.rb` only asserts absolutization for a simple host with no port and no edge cases. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` contains parsing and URL fallback logic (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, plus `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), while `poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests gating and delegation, not parsing/import behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-coverage gap rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.
